Entity: Internal Link Counts / Boilerplate vs Editorial Links
Friction: Every article on this query assumes the internal links exist and asks what you did wrong with them. Two prior questions go unasked: whether the link count you are reading is real, and whether internal links are the constraint at all. Our own audit answered both the hard way — a count of 68 inbound links turned out to be 67 repetitions of one boilerplate component plus 3 editorial links, and the page with 4 inbound links outranked the page with 68 by nine positions.
Logic: Two checks in order, both cheap. First, split the count: crawl inbound links to a target and group by anchor text and containing element. Ours collapsed from 68 to 3 real editorial links once the Related Articles component was excluded, because a component that renders the same anchor and target on every page is one pattern repeated, not 68 votes. Second, test whether links are the binding constraint before optimizing them: our four pages shipped the same day, same cluster, same author, same domain gave a natural control — 68 inbound links ranked 32.1, four inbound links ranked 23.2. Where that leaves you: the audit was worth running because it stopped work, not because it started it. The honest conclusion for a young domain is that authority and cluster depth were the constraint, and internal links were not the thing to spend the week on.
content_angle: A first-party audit that argues against its own subject: the 68-link count was 67 boilerplate repetitions, and even the pages that had real links did not out-rank the page that did not. Publishes the page-level numbers, the same-day same-cluster control group, and the conclusion we actually acted on — stop working on internal links. Contrarian against a genre that only ever prescribes more linking.
author: Marcus Orion
